entries.title: US schema v2 — Intent / Plan / Record / Boundaries
entries.affected_document: section-contracts.md, us-template.md, writing-guide.md, 75× docs/us/, app-desktop validators, migrate_us_v2_structure.py
entries.what_changed: Replaced flat US sections (Acceptance, Context & constraints, Technical implementation, Tests, Out of scope, Notes) with four phase groups: Intent (Acceptance, Why, Where), Plan (refs + Planned), Record (Files/layers + Executed), Boundaries. Migrated all 75 US; validators and monitor protocol updated; legacy aliases removed.
entries.why_changed: Flat H2 siblings mixed create/refine/close content; migration prose piled up; IA and agents could not distinguish intent from delivery record.
entries.impact: All new/refined US must use v2 structure. /complete-us fills ## Record. /refine-us gates on ## Plan. Old headings no longer validated.

entries.title: v2-S5 — board documentation UX (US-0073–0075)
entries.what_changed: Created US-0073 (validate ## Technical implementation in monitor protocol), US-0074 (Doc/Sem doc badge on kanban cards), US-0075 (hide empty columns, collapse frozen by default). Added sprint v2-S5. EPIC-03 reactivated for v2 validation extension.
entries.why_changed: Manager identified gap: ✅ US could lack implementation record with no UI signal; frozen column wastes space when empty. Work must be documented before code per Meridian process.
entries.impact: 75 US on board; v2-S5 runs after or parallel to v2-S4 Should items. Implementation blocked until US reviewed; no code without these acceptance criteria.

entries.title: Product roadmap v3–v6 — epics, sprints, 19 US
entries.affected_document: docs/versions/v3.md–v6.md, docs/epics/EPIC-07–10.md, docs/sprints/v3-S1..v5-S3.md, docs/us/US-0054..0072.md, docs/kanban/board.json, README.md
entries.what_changed: Planned v3 Native Desktop (EPIC-07, Tauri), v4 Authoring Workflows (EPIC-08, extension wizards), v5 Export/Git (EPIC-09, CSV + read-only GitHub), v6 Shared Workspace vision gate (EPIC-10, no US). Created 9 sprints and US-0054–0072 as roadmap backlog. EPIC-04 versions extended to v4.
entries.why_changed: Manager asked to imagine project evolutions ahead of implementation so delivery order and deferred items stay traceable in docs not chat.
entries.impact: 72 US total on board; v3–v5 epics paused until prior version complete. v6 explicitly documentation-only until scope re-approved. Execution still starts at v2 US-0041.

entries.title: v2 sprint plan — 4 sprints, 13 US (US-0041–0053)
entries.affected_document: docs/versions/v2.md, docs/epics/EPIC-05.md, docs/sprints/v2-S1..S4.md, docs/us/US-0041..0053.md, docs/kanban/board.json, docs/README.md
entries.what_changed: Activated v2 and EPIC-05. Created sprints v2-S1 (foundation), v2-S2 (board sync + validate), v2-S3 (create US on disk), v2-S4 (templates + go-live). Added US-0041–0053 including generate_board.py script (US-0044) to fill agent-only board sync gap. EPIC-04 US-0051 adds stale board warning in monitor.
entries.why_changed: v1 complete (40 US); next delivery is VS Code extension with disk writes. Planning needed deterministic script and explicit dependency order before implementation.
entries.impact: v2 status active; EPIC-05 active; 13 new ❌ US on board. Deferred to post-v2: Tauri, marketplace publish, drag kanban, full epic/version wizards. Should US 0050–0051 may ship partial at go-live with manager sign-off.

entries.title: Remove root meridian.md — README + .agent/ only
entries.what_changed: Deleted `meridian.md` at kit repo root. Monorepo onboarding stays in `README.md`; protocol authority is `.agent/MERIDIAN.md`. Client projects copy only `.agent/`. Validator detects kit via `.agent/MERIDIAN.md` instead of `meridian.md`.
entries.why_changed: Two root markdown files duplicated pitch and confused GitHub About vs portable protocol; README is enough for the kit repo.
entries.impact: Install kit with `.agent/` only; agents and workflows no longer fall back to `meridian.md`. Historical US still mention `meridian.md` as past state.

entries.title: Decisions as JSON per day (docs/decisions/)
entries.affected_document: docs/decisions/, 11_decisions.md, .agent/MERIDIAN.md §11.12, skill update-decisions-log, validate_meridian.py, Decisions tab
entries.what_changed: Daily log moves from markdown to JSON: docs/decisions/YYYY-MM-DD.json with entries array (time, title, affected_document, what_changed, why_changed, impact, responsible). New day → new file; same day → prepend in array.
entries.why_changed: Decisions are structured log data — JSON avoids fragile markdown parsing, aligns with board.json, and facilitates UI/validation.
entries.impact: Agents edit JSON; validator requires schema; app renders structured fields without reading markdown.

entries.title: Decisions in folder by date (docs/decisions/)
entries.affected_document: `11_decisions.md` (stub), `docs/decisions/`, `.agent/MERIDIAN.md` §11.12, skill `update-decisions-log`, `validate_meridian.py`, Decisions tab in the app
entries.what_changed: Decision log migrates from monolithic file to **`docs/decisions/YYYY-MM-DD.md`** — one file per day. Entries use `## HH:MM — Title` (time in heading; date in file name). New day → new file; same day → prepend at top of day's file. `11_decisions.md` becomes stub with rules and pointer.
entries.why_changed: Dozens of entries in the same file make reading and editing difficult; date + time organize history and enable dedicated UI.
entries.impact: Agents prepend in `decisions/YYYY-MM-DD.md`; validator requires folder and format; app gains **Decisions** tab to list and read entries.

entries.title: Decision log: new entries at top
entries.what_changed: New decisions are inserted **at the top** of the file (after this title), not at the end. Old entries remain below, intact.
entries.why_changed: Whoever opens the log needs to see current state first; append at end hid recent decisions among dozens of lines.
entries.impact: Agents and skills use prepend; append at end or reordering old entries is forbidden.

entries.title: Delivery only in folders (remove 20_epics and 21_versions indexes)
entries.what_changed: Epics, versions, and sprints are managed **only** in `docs/epics/`, `docs/versions/`, and `docs/sprints/`. Duplicate markdown indexes eliminated. US gate: `05_architecture` approved + referenced epic/version exist in folders.
entries.why_changed: Duplication between index and folders; app already read folders as source of truth (Deliverables/Board).
entries.impact: Skills `create-epic`/`create-version`/`create-sprint` stop updating tables; Setup loses phase 4 as docs 20/21; historical US citing indexes remain as record.

entries.title: Canonical phase order (architecture before epics)
entries.what_changed: `20_epics.md` no longer blocks `05_architecture`; approval of `04` requires `07` approved. UI/kit phases: foundation → principles/releases → architecture → detail → backlog (04) → execution.
entries.why_changed: Get Started and Setup showed epics before architecture — inconsistent with the document → backlog → execute flow.
entries.impact: `/create-epic` and validator enforce gate; `.cursor` mirrors `.agent` via `sync_cursor_kit.sh`.

entries.title: tests / tests_status fields and Planned/Executed checklist
entries.what_changed: Frontmatter gains `tests: required|none` and `tests_status: pending|done|n/a`. **Tests** section mirrors Acceptance: **Planned** (`- [ ]`) + **Executed** (evidence). 🧪 column in monitor = `tests_status: pending`. Prose parsing heuristic removed.
entries.why_changed: Ensure explicit test traceability; avoid false positives/negatives from automatic detector.
entries.impact: US migrated; v0 US closed with `tests_status: done` and evidence in **Executed**.

entries.title: Daily AI workflow (Get Started + `/daily-with-ai`)
entries.what_changed: New section in the Get Started guide (loop orient → contextualize → implement → close → review); `/daily-with-ai` workflow and reference in the kit; docs/README with explicit daily loop.
entries.why_changed: Get Started explained the system but lacked a practical guide for the manager to use AI in Cursor daily.
entries.impact: meridian-routing recognizes daily routine requests; complements `/complete-us` in closing step.

entries.title: US closure with technical implementation (`complete-user-story`)
entries.what_changed: Formalized the post-implementation closure step: skill `complete-user-story`, workflow `/complete-us`, gate in `board-keeper` and done checklist require `## Technical implementation` filled in (files + layers) before `✅`.
entries.why_changed: Traceability between product acceptance and delivered code; avoid US marked done with empty section or only anticipated plan.
entries.impact: Implementing agents must invoke `complete-user-story` when done; existing US in `✅` with shallow section can be enriched on demand.

entries.title: UX v1-S6 (density and focus)
entries.what_changed: Global version filter shared between Deliverables and Board; epic chips cascaded by version; Deliverables with selected version highlighted and others collapsed; compact kanban cards with details in sheet; advanced tools restricted to Setup tab.
entries.why_changed: Visual polish (S3–S5) did not resolve information overload, incoherent filters, and excess nested boxes reported in real use.
entries.impact: EPIC-04 remains `active` (kanban/deliverables still evolving); v2 unchanged.

entries.title: UX v1-S3–S5 and EPIC-06 closure
entries.what_changed: Three visual polish sprints after functional MVP: data on board/deliverables (S3), tokens and progress (S4), Setup and advanced tools (S5). EPIC-06 marked `complete`.
entries.why_changed: Manager needed coherent interface before considering v1 'presentable'; loose zinc and inconsistent cards hindered daily reading.
entries.impact: v2 and EPIC-05 remain `planned`/`paused`; next milestone is VSCode bridge, not more v1 reading polish.

entries.title: Versions and sprints in files (`docs/versions/`, `docs/sprints/`)
entries.affected_document: `21_versions.md`, `docs/versions/v*.md`, `docs/sprints/*.md`, `parser.ts`, `project-loader.ts`, `validate_meridian.py`, skills `create-version`/`create-sprint`, Get Started guide, Deliverables tab
entries.what_changed: Releases migrated from monolithic sections in `21_versions.md` to `docs/versions/vX.md`; sprints to `docs/sprints/vX-SY.md`. `21_versions.md` became phase index. US references `version: vX`; validator requires corresponding file.
entries.why_changed: Symmetry with epics/US, clarity for AI (`/create-version`, `/plan-sprint`), and roadmap scale.
entries.impact: Workflows `/create-version`, new skills; sprint-planner and create-user-story updated.

entries.title: User story IDs with 4 digits (`US-XXXX`)
entries.what_changed: Fixed ID format `US-XXXX` (four digits, zero-padded). Files renamed (`US-001.md` → `US-0001.md`). File name must match `id` in frontmatter.
entries.why_changed: Catalog scale — avoids visual collision and keeps lexicographic order aligned with numeric up to US-9999.
entries.impact: Historical entries in this log keep old nomenclature where cited; operational references use new format.

entries.title: Enriched epic model (`outcome`, anatomy)
entries.what_changed: Epic now requires `outcome` in frontmatter and structured sections (Capability, Expected Outcome, Out of this epic). US references epic only by `epic: EPIC-XX` — canonical epic source is `docs/epics/`. New skill `create-epic`.
entries.why_changed: Separate product capability concept (epic) from executable task (US) and give clear 'done' criteria at product level.
entries.impact: Python validator and TS parser require `outcome`; agents documentation-strategist, sprint-planner, process-manager and board-keeper updated.

entries.title: Epics in individual files (`docs/epics/`)
entries.what_changed: Each epic moved from a section in `20_epics.md` to its own file in `docs/epics/EPIC-XX.md` with YAML frontmatter (like user stories). `20_epics.md` became a phase index with summary table. App and validator read the `epics/` folder.
entries.why_changed: Symmetry with `docs/us/`, less parallel edit conflict, structured frontmatter, and scale as catalog grows.
entries.impact: US creation gate still requires `20_epics.md` + `21_versions.md` approved; US reference `epic:` that must exist in `docs/epics/`.

entries.title: UX v1-S2 (EPIC-06)
entries.what_changed: Epic **EPIC-06** and sprint **v1-S2** with onboarding (`WelcomeScreen`), single bar (`MonitorTopBar`), Setup/Deliverables/Board tabs, collapsible alerts, lean kanban, Python validation in advanced tools.
entries.why_changed: v1 delivered function but UI was confusing and unfriendly to manager.
entries.impact: Future UX iterations may become v1-S3 or v2 criteria; does not block EPIC-05.

entries.title: Go-live v1-S1 (Folder Monitor MVP)
entries.what_changed: v1-S1 marked complete with go-live checklist; `05_architecture.md` → `approved` (monitored folder = `docs/`); EPIC-02 → `complete`; board regenerated from US.
entries.why_changed: Close v1 milestone before planning v2 (VSCode / writes).
entries.impact: Next product work goes in `21_versions` v2 section and new US under EPIC-05.

entries.title: Monitored folder = `docs/` (not repository root)
entries.what_changed: The File System Access API opens directly the project's **docs/** folder (`00_scope.md` at the handle root, `us/`, `kanban/`). Validation no longer requires a `docs/` subfolder inside the selected root. Loader and phase reader read files at the handle root. Issue messages use paths relative to the docs folder (`20_epics.md`, `us/US-001.md`).
entries.why_changed: All Meridian structure that manager edits with agents lives in `docs/`; opening repository or `app-desktop/` was wrong concept for dogfooding.
entries.impact: `validate_meridian.py` in dev still receives app root (`app-desktop/`), not only `docs/`. US-015 unchanged on this point.

entries.title: Inline reading of docs 00–11 (US-017)
entries.what_changed: Capability to **read each initial setup `.md`** in the app (Read .md button + frontmatter/content panel). Registered as **US-017** in epic **EPIC-02**, not as a separate epic — it is part of the setup monitor.
entries.why_changed: Manager needs to review documents in the same tool that monitors the flow, not just see aggregated status.
entries.impact: US-010 should reuse `splitFrontmatter` / reader; US-011 focuses list status from parser.

entries.title: Monitor product model and v1 backlog
entries.what_changed: Epics EPIC-02/03/04 redefined for the three tabs (Initial setup, Epics, Kanban + validations). EPIC-01 marked complete. Created US-008 (v0 shell) and US-009–US-016 (v1-S1: real folder, parser, tabs, validations, end of mock). US-002 reopened as 🔶 until real reading (US-011). Source of truth remains Markdown; app becomes reader in v1, not author. Tasks/Bug/Spike do not become artifacts — technical work stays in **Technical implementation** inside the US.
entries.why_changed: Align product with agent use (dogfooding in `app-desktop/docs`) without replicating Jira; eliminate confusing UI (two status/flow columns).
entries.impact: 05_architecture.md should go to review with parser and File System Access; README docs; agents must cite US before coding v1.

entries.title: `.agent` kit aligned to Antigravity standard
entries.what_changed: Created `README.md` at the repository root; `rules/MERIDIAN.md` now uses `trigger: always_on`; added `meridian-routing`, `skills/doc.md`, `references/` in skills, operational agents with phases, workflows with `$ARGUMENTS`, and updated `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
entries.why_changed: Kit needs same operational depth as Antigravity (progressive disclosure, routing, gates) adapted to Meridian documentation governance, not just empty folders.
entries.impact: app-desktop/docs (US-007, README, 00_scope, 21_versions, 05_architecture), board.json and app validation.

entries.title: `skills/` folder was removed
entries.what_changed: Root `skills/` folder was removed. Skills now exist only as formal packages in `.agent/skills/{skill}/SKILL.md`.
entries.why_changed: `.agent/`-based structure is more complete and allows organizing agents, skills, workflows, rules, and scripts in a single operational layer for agents.
entries.impact: 00_scope.md, 21_versions.md, US-005.md, US-006.md, board.json and `.agent/MERIDIAN.md`.

entries.title: Agent operational layer uses `.agent`
entries.what_changed: Agent structure was organized in `.agent/`, with subfolders for agents, skills, workflows, rules, and scripts.
entries.why_changed: Meridian needs a reusable operational layer for agents, separate from visual app and more structured than loose skills at root.
entries.impact: 00_scope.md, 21_versions.md, skills/README.md and future desktop app validations.

entries.title: Agent skills enter the protocol
entries.what_changed: Root `skills/` folder was created with auxiliary instructions for agents and protocol security section was deepened.
entries.why_changed: Meridian needs to separate visual app management and operational guidance for agents. Skills help agents execute recurring tasks without inflating app home or depending on a visual tool.
entries.impact: 00_scope.md, 21_versions.md and future desktop app validations.

entries.title: Protocol and desktop app were separated
entries.what_changed: `meridian.md` became the universal protocol for AI agents, while the Vite app and its documentation were separated into `app-desktop/`.
entries.why_changed: Protocol needs to be copyable to any project, and desktop app should only be a visual layer that opens and monitors a Meridian folder.
entries.impact: README.md, 21_versions.md, and the app's home screen.

entries.title: Git and local quality enter foundation
entries.what_changed: The project started using Git from the foundation, `.gitignore` to protect local files, Prettier, Husky, and lint-staged.
entries.why_changed: Meridian flow requires consistency and governance before accelerating implementation with AI agents.
entries.impact: 02_security.md, 04_principles.md and 08_environments.md.

entries.title: shadcn must be installed via official CLI
entries.what_changed: Visual base must use official shadcn installer to generate components.
entries.why_changed: Project must follow library expected flow and avoid manually recreated shadcn components.
entries.impact: 04_principles.md and the Vite app implementation.

entries.title: Meridian is a flow for development with AI agents
entries.what_changed: Scope was updated to explicitly declare that Meridian is built for the new era of working with AI agents.
entries.why_changed: Central product point is allowing people to manage development with agents while maintaining context, control, visibility, and consistency.
entries.impact: 03_user_types.md, 04_principles.md and future Vite app screens.

entries.title: Meridian prioritizes consistent development
entries.what_changed: Positioning was expanded to anyone, dev, team, or area wanting to conduct development with a pragmatic SDD-based flow.
entries.why_changed: Meridian should not be treated as tool only for small teams nor as an agent mesh. Product exists to give visibility, control, and consistency to the process manager.
entries.impact: 03_user_types.md, 20_epics.md, 21_versions.md and meridian.md.

entries.title: Canonical board will be JSON
entries.what_changed: Board generated by Meridian now has `board.json` as canonical format. CSV no longer part of base structure.
entries.why_changed: Vite app and future extension need to operate on rich stable structure; exports like CSV should be derived on demand, not maintained as parallel source.
entries.impact: README.md, 21_versions.md and future architecture documentation.

entries.title: First app will be Vite before extension
entries.what_changed: First delivery will be a local Vite app with React, TypeScript, and shadcn/ui.
entries.why_changed: A Vite app allows validating experience, documentation rules, and visual structure before investing in VSCode extension.
entries.impact: 00_scope.md, 01_tech_stack.md, 20_epics.md, 21_versions.md and 05_architecture.md.

entries.title: Meridian starts following its own flow
entries.what_changed: Project will be developed using Meridian structure from the start.
entries.why_changed: Product needs to prove its living documentation flow while being built.
entries.impact: Creation of `app-desktop/docs` folder and Phase 0 documents for desktop app.
